question: What is one of the most immediate, life-threatening dangers after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Severe hemorrhage
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Permanent hypertension
options.D: Chronic hair loss

explanation: You nailed it! Heavy bleeding from incomplete tissue removal or trauma is a leading cause of emergency admissions and death after unsafe procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h3)

question: Which professionals are typically part of the multidisciplinary team for a child with a learning disability?

options.A: Cardiologists, physiotherapists, and dietitians only
options.B: Radiologists, lab technicians, and hospital accountants
options.C: Nurses, educational psychologists, and speech therapists
options.D: Surgeons, pharmacists, and hospital administrators only

explanation: A collaborative team approach involves health and educational specialists working together to support the child's specific needs. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h8)

question: What is a major social reason families continue to practice FGM?

options.A: Compliance with international health mandates
options.B: A direct recommendation by the national medical association
options.C: The prevention of childhood infectious diseases
options.D: Fear of social exclusion and unmarriageability

explanation: Sadly, many families do it because they fear their daughters will be rejected by the community or struggle to find husbands. Understanding this helps you treat patients with empathy. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why should you avoid giving rectal medications to a patient who has active rectal bleeding?

options.A: The patient will automatically develop an allergic reaction to the drug
options.B: The medication can worsen mucosal damage and might be washed away
options.C: The drug will bypass the liver entirely and cause immediate toxicity
options.D: The rectal sphincter will permanently lock shut and trap the medicine

explanation: Active bleeding or severe diarrhea stops the drug from being absorbed properly and can hurt the already irritated tissues. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a main job of the gonads?

options.A: Quickly fixing sudden drops in blood pressure
options.B: Supporting secondary sex traits like body hair
options.C: Helping with reproductive growth
options.D: Producing sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone

explanation: Spot on! Gonads focus on reproductive hormones. Blood pressure is managed by other organs like your kidneys and heart. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h6)

question: What would happen if the hypothalamus released GnRH in a steady, continuous stream instead of in pulses?

options.A: It would make the pituitary gland grow larger in size
options.B: It would immediately trigger strong bone growth in the arms
options.C: It would stop reproductive stimulation instead of promoting it
options.D: It would cause puberty to happen twice as fast

explanation: Exactly! The pituitary gland needs short, repeating pulses of GnRH to stay active. If the signal is non-stop, it actually shuts the process down. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T13#GNS121_U5_T13_h2)

question: What is a major downside of a healthcare system that focuses only on big hospitals?

options.A: It provides too many vaccines directly inside family homes
options.B: It neglects preventive care and ignores rural or poor communities
options.C: It focuses too much on keeping people healthy
options.D: It relies entirely on community health workers instead of doctors

explanation: Exactly. When everything is locked inside city hospitals, people in remote areas miss out on basic checkups and early care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of community entry in the mobilisation cycle?

options.A: Collecting taxes from local market traders
options.B: Building a permanent health clinic building
options.C: Conducting mass vaccinations for all children
options.D: Gaining social and legal acceptance from local leaders

explanation: Community entry is all about introducing yourself, getting permission, and building trust with local leaders before starting any work. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h3)

question: How does disease surveillance differ from standard bedside nursing care?

options.A: Surveillance is only performed by doctors inside specialized laboratories
options.B: Surveillance deals exclusively with chronic genetic disorders
options.C: Surveillance requires advanced surgical skills instead of basic bedside observation
options.D: Surveillance focuses on population-level health trends rather than single patients

explanation: While bedside nursing cares for one patient at a time, surveillance looks at the big picture to protect entire communities. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h1)

question: A patient uses crushed fresh leaves on a swollen joint. What kind of poultice is this?

options.A: An herbal poultice
options.B: A surgical poultice
options.C: A chemical poultice
options.D: A synthetic poultice

explanation: Using fresh plants or leaves directly falls under the category of traditional herbal poultices. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which family planning method gives you dual protection against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Subdermal implants
options.B: Oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Intrauterine devices
options.D: Condoms

explanation: That's right! Barrier methods like male and female condoms block both sperm and infections, making them the only modern contraceptives that offer dual protection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h3)

question: Why does a large pleural effusion cause difficulty breathing?

options.A: The accumulated fluid compresses the lung tissue and limits expansion
options.B: The fluid forces the heart to pump blood too fast into the lungs
options.C: The excess fluid directly blocks the upper airway passages
options.D: The fluid creates an infection that stops red blood cells from carrying oxygen

explanation: Fluid taking up space in the chest cavity prevents the lung from fully expanding during inhalation, leading to shortness of breath. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h1)

question: What is the main trap when relying on routine blood tests to check mineral levels like calcium or magnesium?

options.A: Labs cannot measure minerals accurately in human blood.
options.B: Mineral levels change drastically every five minutes.
options.C: Blood levels may stay normal even when tissue stores are low.
options.D: Minerals break down instantly when exposed to room air.

explanation: The body is smart—it will pull minerals out of your bones and tissues to keep the blood levels looking normal, which can easily trick you! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T005#GNS227_U5_T005_h4)

question: A 55-year-old patient has a 10-year history of poorly controlled high blood pressure. What major condition are they at high risk for?

options.A: Chronic kidney stones
options.B: Cerebrovascular accident
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Degenerative joint disease

explanation: You nailed it! Years of high pressure wear down cerebral blood vessels, putting the patient at high risk for a stroke (cerebrovascular accident). [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h3)

question: A patient living near a fast-flowing river in a rural Nigerian community presents with severe skin irritation and failing eyesight. Which endemic disease is most likely causing this?

options.A: Lassa fever
options.B: Onchocerciasis
options.C: Acute malaria
options.D: Typhoid fever

explanation: Onchocerciasis, also known as river blindness, is transmitted by blackflies living near fast-flowing rivers and causes skin lesions and vision impairment. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h3)

question: An older patient looks at their adult child to answer all your health questions. What should you do first?

options.A: Refuse to continue the visit until the child leaves the room
options.B: Acknowledge the family decision-maker while keeping the patient engaged
options.C: Document that the patient is mentally incompetent
options.D: Ignore the child and force the patient to answer alone

explanation: In many Nigerian homes, family members share in health decisions. Respect the family structure while gently inviting the patient to join the conversation too. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h3)

question: During a blood transfusion, a patient suddenly gets back pain, chills, and fever. What is your very first action?

options.A: Call the hospital laboratory to double-check the patient's name
options.B: Stop the transfusion immediately and disconnect the tubing
options.C: Slow down the infusion rate and grab a warm cotton blanket
options.D: Administer a dose of oral paracetamol for the rising fever

explanation: Stop it right away! Cutting off the flow prevents any more incompatible blood from harming your patient during a reaction. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h6)

question: Where do the coronary arteries get their blood supply from?

options.A: The main upper vein (superior vena cava)
options.B: The left upper chamber
options.C: The pulmonary artery
options.D: The base of the aorta

explanation: The heart muscle works non-stop and needs its own fuel supply! It takes the very first branches right off the aorta where the oxygen-rich blood leaves the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h6)

question: What factor has the biggest influence on the overall survival outlook for a patient with a vulval tumour?

options.A: The stage of the cancer at the time of diagnosis
options.B: The specific brand of dressing used on the wound
options.C: The patient's personal preference for radiation therapy
options.D: The exact age of the patient during surgery

explanation: Well done! Catching the cancer early, before it spreads to the lymph nodes, gives the patient the best chance at long-term survival. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h8)

question: A patient is diagnosed with glaucoma caused by blocked fluid drainage in the front of the eye. What fluid is building up?

options.A: Blood plasma
options.B: Lacrimal fluid
options.C: Vitreous humor
options.D: Aqueous humor

explanation: Aqueous humor is the watery fluid in the anterior segment whose blockage leads to increased pressure in glaucoma. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why do we quickly set up large-bore IV lines for a woman experiencing heavy postpartum bleeding?

options.A: To make it easier to administer oral painkillers and antibiotics
options.B: To prevent the patient from moving her limbs around too much
options.C: To measure the exact temperature of blood flowing through the veins
options.D: To allow rapid infusion of emergency fluids and blood replacement

explanation: Big veins and wide needles let IV fluids and blood rush in fast to fight off shock when a mother is bleeding out. Every second counts! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T013#GNS226_U1_T013_h6)

question: Which group of patients is most often affected by drug under-prescription?

options.A: Children admitted for acute infectious diseases
options.B: Young healthy adults visiting emergency rooms
options.C: Athletes recovering from orthopedic surgeries
options.D: Older adults and those with multiple chronic illnesses

explanation: Spot on! Older patients and those with complex health issues often miss out on necessary care because healthcare providers worry too much about drug interactions. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T8#GNS215_U1_T8_h2)

question: What are the two big features that define all stem cells?

options.A: Programmed death and shrinkage
options.B: Rapid mutation and anaplasia
options.C: Self-renewal and potency
options.D: Encapsulation and metastasis

explanation: Spot on! Stem cells are amazing because they can both make copies of themselves (self-renewal) and turn into specialized cells (potency). [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h4)

question: What do high-pressure alarms usually tell you about a mechanically ventilated patient?

options.A: The patient is breathing too slowly or not at all
options.B: Changes in lung compliance or increased airway resistance
options.C: A disconnection of the main tubing from the patient
options.D: A power failure in the wall electrical socket

explanation: When the high-pressure alarm sounds, it means something is making it harder to push air in—like mucus plugs, coughing, or the patient biting the tube. Time to put on your detective hat and check the patient! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h4)

question: What is a major error a nurse can make during community mobilisation?

options.A: Asking local leaders for permission to enter the village
options.B: Taking over leadership and making decisions for the community
options.C: Teaching mothers how to prepare oral rehydration salt
options.D: Working with local volunteers to clean up the environment

explanation: Nurses should facilitate and empower, not take control and rob the community of their self-reliance. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)

question: When is skeletal traction usually taken off?

options.A: When the patient is ready for surgery, casting, or healing allows
options.B: As soon as the patient gets bored on bed rest
options.C: When the pin site develops normal crusting
options.D: Exactly 24 hours after the pin was put in

explanation: You got it! Skeletal traction is a temporary helper. It comes off once definitive care like surgery or a cast takes over, or when the bone is stable enough. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T9#GNS221_U1_T9_h6)

question: You need to draw routine blood from a patient who has an IV line running in their left forearm. What should you do?

options.A: Use a butterfly needle to draw blood from the hand on the same side
options.B: Draw the blood specimen from the opposite uninfused arm
options.C: Turn off the intravenous infusion for two minutes and draw from above the site
options.D: Draw the sample directly through the running intravenous catheter

explanation: Always avoid drawing blood from an arm with an active IV. The IV fluids will dilute your sample and give you completely inaccurate lab numbers! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h7)

question: How does family planning directly help safe motherhood efforts?

options.A: By eliminating all natural causes of infertility
options.B: By helping women space pregnancies to protect their physical recovery
options.C: By ensuring women have children as rapidly as possible
options.D: By replacing the need for antenatal clinic attendance

explanation: Spacing kids gives mum's body a well-deserved break to build back her blood levels and strength before the next journey. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T001#GNS226_U1_T001_h6)

question: A quiet elderly patient takes a normal sedative before a procedure and suddenly starts shouting. What is your best conclusion?

options.A: The medication dosage was clearly too low to be effective
options.B: The patient has developed an anaphylactic immune reaction
options.C: The patient is experiencing a rare idiosyncratic drug response
options.D: The patient is suffering from acute bacterial meningitis

explanation: Getting wild instead of sleepy from a sedative points right to a paradoxical idiosyncratic reaction. Spot on! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T7#GNS125_U1_T7_h4)

question: An advanced HIV patient comes in with distinct purplish skin lesions and ongoing watery diarrhea. What are those skin spots called?

options.A: Oral candidiasis
options.B: Toxoplasmosis
options.C: Kaposi sarcoma
options.D: Herpes zoster

explanation: You're doing great. Those telltale purplish or brownish skin lesions are known as Kaposi sarcoma, a cancer linked to HIV. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h3)

question: What is a major difference between normal postpartum blues and postpartum depression?

options.A: Postpartum blues resolve on their own within two weeks
options.B: Postpartum depression appears on the first day after delivery
options.C: Postpartum depression only affects women who had cesarean births
options.D: Postpartum depression require immediate psychiatric admission

explanation: The 'baby blues' are mild and usually fade away within a couple of weeks without special treatment, whereas postpartum depression is heavier, lasts longer, and needs real support. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h6)

question: What is a key nursing duty when caring for a patient with a metabolic disorder?

options.A: Encouraging the patient to eat unlimited amounts of simple sugars
options.B: Prescribing new metabolic medications to cure the underlying defect
options.C: Replacing all oral nutrition with intravenous fluids permanently
options.D: Monitoring laboratory results and tracking dietary intake closely

explanation: As a nurse, keeping a close eye on lab trends and meals helps you catch sneaky metabolic imbalances before they become emergencies! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h8)

question: A community nurse sets up a free blood pressure check station in the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Quaternary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: You're doing great! Screening checks (like blood pressure tests) catch problems early so treatment can start before things get worse. That is secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of doing regular mental health checks on these patients?

options.A: To prove that the family is doing a poor job at home
options.B: To test the patient's physical strength and walking balance
options.C: To find a permanent cure for the underlying genetic mutation
options.D: To catch subtle shifts in mood and thinking early and guide care

explanation: Spot on! Catching small mental changes early helps nurses update safety plans and support systems before things get overwhelming. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h4)

question: A patient lies quietly with closed eyes, but opens them right away when you call their name loudly. What is their eye score?
explanation: Spot on! When they open their eyes only after you speak to them or call their name, that's a score of 3. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T7#GNS222_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why do clinical nurses need to understand the basics of diet and nutrition?

options.A: It allows nurses to support recovery and identify early malnutrition
options.B: It helps nurses prescribe complex surgical procedures independently
options.C: It replaces the need for professional hospital dietitians entirely
options.D: It enables nurses to manufacture synthetic vitamins at the bedside

explanation: Knowing your nutrition helps you spot early signs of poor feeding in patients and guide them toward a faster recovery! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h1)

question: What usually causes a Bartholin duct cyst to form?

options.A: Hormonal overproduction by the adrenal cortex
options.B: Blockage of the gland duct causing fluid to back up
options.C: Direct bacterial invasion from the urinary bladder
options.D: A genetic absence of the external genitalia glands

explanation: When the tiny tube (duct) leading from the Bartholin gland gets blocked, the fluid has nowhere to go and builds up into a cyst. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h2)

question: What is a common result when a primary breadwinner develops a disabling chronic illness?

options.A: Automatic government provision of permanent housing
options.B: The complete elimination of domestic chores
options.C: Shifts in household roles and financial responsibilities
options.D: Immediate improvement in overall family communication

explanation: A major illness forces other family members to take over tasks previously managed by the sick individual. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: A patient with chronic bowel inflammation passes pale, bulky, foul-smelling stools that float. What nutritional problem does this suggest?

options.A: Fat malabsorption due to impaired intestinal function.
options.B: A sudden increase in stomach acid production.
options.C: Excessive intake of dietary fiber and green vegetables.
options.D: Rapid dehydration caused by drinking too little water.

explanation: Pale, bulky, and foul-smelling stools that float indicate steatorrhea, which means fats are not being absorbed properly in the gut. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h4)

question: What common side effects of metronidazole should you warn your patient about so they don't panic?

options.A: Permanent yellowing of the skin and eyes
options.B: Complete loss of the sense of smell
options.C: Metallic taste and dark-colored urine
options.D: Sudden swelling of the hands and feet

explanation: A metal taste in the mouth and darker urine can look scary to a patient, but it's totally normal with metronidazole. Giving a quick heads-up saves them a lot of worry! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h4)

question: Why should patients always be involved in setting their own rehabilitation goals?

options.A: It ensures the recovery targets matter to the patient's actual daily life.
options.B: It completely removes the need for physical therapy oversight.
options.C: Hospital accreditation rules legally prohibit nurse-only care plans.
options.D: Patients have medical degrees that guide clinical interventions.

explanation: Exactly! When patients help choose what they want to achieve, they feel more motivated to push through tough therapy sessions. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h2)

question: Why is bone considered an important storage bank for the whole body?

options.A: It burns stored fat tissue to maintain a stable body temperature
options.B: It produces hormones that regulate the speed of digestion
options.C: It filters waste products directly out of the circulating blood supply
options.D: It stores large amounts of essential minerals like calcium and phosphorus

explanation: Bones hold onto key minerals and release them into the blood whenever your nerves and muscles need them. Perfect! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why can transitioning from a hospital to home care be tough for a nurse?

options.A: Hospitals use entirely different medical terminology.
options.B: Hospitals do not teach any clinical procedures.
options.C: Home care requires autonomous decision-making without immediate medical backup.
options.D: Nurses in hospitals never interact with patients directly.

explanation: Correct! In the hospital, doctors and senior colleagues are close by. In home care, you often have to think and act independently. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T9#GNS324_U1_T9_h4)

question: What is a 'double-barreled' question in a research survey?

options.A: A question placed at the very end of a long research tool
options.B: A single question that mistakenly asks about two different things
options.C: A question that offers more than five possible answer choices
options.D: A survey item written in two different languages at once

explanation: Double-barreled questions confuse respondents because they cannot give separate answers to two different ideas packed into one sentence. You'll master questionnaire design in no time! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h3)

question: Which body tissue burns the most calories even when you are completely at rest?

options.A: Lean muscle tissue
options.B: Fibrous connective tissue
options.C: Subcutaneous fat tissue
options.D: Visceral adipose tissue

explanation: Muscles are metabolically active! Lean muscle requires much more energy to maintain day-to-day than stored body fat does. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T9#GNS121_U1_T9_h2)

question: Which of these is usually one of the very first warning signs that a patient is slipping into shock?

options.A: Restlessness and increased heart rate
options.B: Elevated blood pressure and flushed face
options.C: Slow, bounding pulse and warm skin
options.D: High urine output and deep sleep

explanation: When blood flow dips, the body panics a bit and pumps harder (tachycardia) while the brain gets restless from lack of oxygen. Always trust your instincts when a patient suddenly seems 'off'! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h7)

question: What should a cataract surgery patient wear while sleeping during early recovery?

options.A: A rigid protective eye shield
options.B: A dark pair of polarized sunglasses
options.C: A sterile moist gauze dressing
options.D: A tight elastic pressure bandage

explanation: Wearing a hard shield to bed ensures the patient doesn't accidentally rub or press on their healing eye while fast asleep. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T3#GNS311_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why is developing a fever especially dangerous for a child right after they recover from cardiac arrest?

options.A: It stops all medications from working
options.B: It automatically triggers another cardiac arrest
options.C: It increases the metabolic demand of the injured brain
options.D: It proves the resuscitation attempt failed entirely

explanation: When a child's brain is recovering from lack of oxygen, a fever forces it to work much harder and use up oxygen it simply doesn't have to spare. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why would a nurse need to flush or irrigate a patient's ear?

options.A: To drain excessive fluid from the middle ear cavity
options.B: To remove stuck earwax or small foreign objects
options.C: To repair a torn eardrum using pressurized water
options.D: To treat an active bacterial infection deep in the inner ear

explanation: Ear irrigation is a safe way to wash out stubborn wax buildup or little things that got stuck in the outer ear. Great clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h1)

question: What main event causes urine to leak out in stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Complete blockage of the urethra
options.B: An overactive detrusor muscle spasm
options.C: A sudden urinary tract infection
options.D: Sudden physical pressure on the bladder

explanation: You've got this! Stress incontinence happens when sudden physical pressure—like coughing, laughing, or lifting—pushes urine out because the bladder pressure beats the urethra's grip. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h1)

question: Why should you clean a wound surface with sterile saline before taking a swab for culture?

options.A: To dissolve the stitches holding the wound edges together
options.B: To completely sterilize the interior of the wound
options.C: To numb the local pain receptors in the damaged tissue
options.D: To remove surface contaminants and dead skin cells

explanation: Wiping away surface debris ensures you are culturing the actual infection deep down, rather than just the dust and dead cells on top. [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h5)

question: Why do patients with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus pee so often (polyuria)?

options.A: Direct irritation of the bladder wall by circulating ketone bodies
options.B: High blood glucose pulling water into the urine through osmotic diuresis
options.C: Failure of the pituitary gland to release antidiuretic hormone
options.D: Rapid fluid shifts caused by sudden peripheral muscle wasting

explanation: When there is too much sugar in the blood, the kidneys try to filter it out. Sugar acts like a sponge, pulling extra water right along with it into the urine—leading to lots of trips to the restroom! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h5)

question: Why are people with long-term HIV at a higher risk for heart disease?

options.A: Patients universally develop severe iron-deficiency anemia
options.B: Low red blood cell counts force the heart to beat faster
options.C: Persistent systemic inflammation damages blood vessels
options.D: The virus directly destroys heart muscle tissue daily

explanation: Ongoing immune activation keeps the body in a state of low-level inflammation, which over time can damage blood vessels and raise heart disease risk. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T13#GNS216_U6_T13_h5)

question: Which injection site symptom means the patient needs to call a doctor right away?

options.A: A small pinprick dot of dry blood on the skin surface
options.B: Pus drainage, severe pain, and spreading warmth
options.C: Temporary slight coolness where the alcohol dried
options.D: Mild fading skin discoloration from a tiny bruise

explanation: Those are classic red flags for an infection! Pus, severe pain, and warmth mean the site needs medical attention quickly. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h7)

question: How is the malaria parasite (Plasmodium) most commonly spread in Nigeria?

options.A: Inhalation of airborne droplets
options.B: Bite of the female Anopheles mosquito
options.C: Ingestion of poorly washed vegetables
options.D: Direct person-to-person skin contact

explanation: You've got this! Infected female Anopheles mosquitoes carry the malaria parasite and pass it into the bloodstream when they bite. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T5#GNS223_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why do inhaled toxic gases enter the bloodstream so quickly?

options.A: Inhaled toxins bypass the liver entirely and go straight to peripheral tissues.
options.B: The alveolar-capillary membrane is extremely thin and has a massive surface area.
options.C: Lungs actively pump foreign gases into red blood cells using ATP energy.
options.D: Gases immediately convert into water-soluble ions inside the upper airway.

explanation: The lungs are built for fast gas exchange! Their huge surface area and super-thin tissue barrier let gases diffuse right into the blood with almost no delay. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h2)

question: Which of these can act as a reservoir where germs live?

options.A: Completely dry and sunny metal surfaces
options.B: Sterile surgical instruments only
options.C: Soil, water, humans, and animals
options.D: Intact human skin with no normal flora

explanation: Germs aren't picky! They can live inside living hosts like humans and animals, or in the environment like soil and water. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the most important ingredient for any healthcare team to work well together?

options.A: Strict orders given only by physicians
options.B: Independent work without sharing notes
options.C: Focusing solely on hospital procedures
options.D: Mutual respect among all team members

explanation: Great thinking! Teamwork only works when everyone values what each person brings to the table. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h2)

question: Why is it helpful to ask about the exact kind of pain a patient has, like whether it feels burning or sharp?

options.A: It proves to the medical team that the patient is telling the truth
options.B: It is required by hospital insurance companies before giving drugs
options.C: It prevents the patient from feeling anxious about their diagnosis
options.D: It helps identify the underlying cause, like nerve or bone involvement

question: Why is it smart to involve traditional birth attendants (TBAs) in community safe motherhood programs?

options.C: Parasites
options.D: Bacteriophages

explanation: Spot on! Viruses (like rhinoviruses) are the culprits behind the vast majority of our everyday coughs and colds. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h1)

question: How can clinical nurses positively influence waste management practices on their wards?

options.A: By writing national environmental laws in parliament
options.B: By driving the municipal garbage trucks on weekends
options.C: By buying new incineration machines for the hospital
options.D: By acting as role models and teaching junior staff correct sorting

explanation: Spot on! Your daily good habits teach junior colleagues and students how to do things the right way. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h7)

question: Why is general inspection a great first step before doing a physical exam on a patient with a blood disorder?

options.A: It provides a quick way to measure the exact red blood cell count
options.B: It replaces the need to check laboratory blood test results completely
options.C: It is the only legal way to diagnose leukemia in the ward
options.D: It helps spot immediate signs of distress, fatigue, and distress clues

explanation: Looking at your patient first gives you a quick overall picture of their energy level, comfort, and obvious physical symptoms before you dive into detailed touching and listening. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T3#GNS311_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the purpose of an EMR audit trail?

options.A: To automatically record every time a user opens or views a patient chart
options.B: To measure how fast a patient recovers from surgery
options.C: To monitor how many steps a nurse walks during a 12-hour shift
options.D: To track how much money the hospital spends on computer maintenance

explanation: An audit trail leaves a digital footprint, tracking who looked at a patient's file and exactly when they opened it. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h5)

question: Which neonatal complication is commonly linked to fetal hyperinsulinemia delaying lung maturation?

options.A: Respiratory distress syndrome
options.B: Neonatal jaundice
options.C: Congenital heart murmurs
options.D: Necrotizing enterocolitis

explanation: High insulin levels can delay the production of lung surfactant, putting the newborn at a higher risk for respiratory distress syndrome. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h7)

question: A patient asks how to prevent stomach upset during stressful exams. What is your best response?

options.A: Tell the patient that stress has no impact on digestion
options.B: Suggest taking heavy sleeping pills during the daytime hours
options.C: Encourage stress reduction techniques and regular balanced meals
options.D: Advise the patient to stop eating completely until stress ends

explanation: Stress really does mess with your tummy! Helping patients manage stress and stick to regular meals protects their gut from acting up. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by community midwives in rural Nigeria?

options.A: Insecure terrain and difficult geographical transportation routes
options.B: Irregular salary payments and financial delay issues
options.C: Professional isolation due to working alone in remote outposts
options.D: Immediate access to fully equipped advanced intensive care units

explanation: Rural community midwives lack access to advanced intensive care units; their reality is marked by resource limitations and isolation, not surplus equipment. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h8)

question: Why can untreated vaginal infections sometimes lead to fertility problems?

options.A: Infections can ascend into the upper reproductive tract and cause scarring.
options.B: Vaginal pH permanently drops to zero, destroying all gametes.
options.C: Inflammation triggers the immediate closure of the vaginal canal.
options.D: Pathogens consume all systemic estrogen needed for ovulation.

explanation: You nailed it! If ignored, germs can travel upward into the uterus and fallopian tubes, causing inflammation and scar tissue that can make getting pregnant harder later. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h7)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should check before moving a patient to a chair?

options.A: The color of the patient's room walls
options.B: The brand name of the hospital bed
options.C: The patient's current ability to bear weight
options.D: The exact time the doctor's shift ends

explanation: Always check if the patient can stand or support themselves first! This tells you if you need an extra pair of hands or a mechanical lift. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: When a dementia patient suddenly acts out or becomes aggressive, what is this most often a sign of?

options.A: A direct side effect of drinking too much water
options.B: A deliberate attempt to upset family members
options.C: An unmet physical need or reaction to distress
options.D: A permanent change in their core personality

explanation: Behavior is communication! When they can't say 'I'm in pain' or 'I'm scared,' they might lash out instead. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h5)

question: What is the hallmark warning sign of placenta previa?

options.A: Painless, bright red vaginal bleeding
options.B: Sudden swelling of the face and hands
options.C: High fever and foul-smelling discharge
options.D: Severe sharp pain with a rigid abdomen

explanation: Think of placenta previa as the placenta lying low near the cervix. When it bleeds, it's typically painless and bright red—a classic sign to watch out for on the ward! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a general physical examination?

options.A: To diagnose complex psychiatric disorders independently
options.B: To replace the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.C: To prescribe appropriate pharmacological interventions
options.D: To gather baseline data about a patient's health status

explanation: A general exam is primarily done to establish a baseline of physical health so nurses can track changes over time. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary tool used in tele-nursing to deliver care?

options.A: Information and communication technologies
options.B: Surgical instruments and sterile trays
options.C: Laboratory reagents and microscopy
options.D: Manual blood pressure cuffs and stethoscopes

explanation: Tele-nursing relies fundamentally on electronic communication tools like phones and computers to reach patients remotely. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h1)

question: A patient stops taking their prescribed tuberculosis medication because it makes them feel nauseated every morning. What kind of barrier does this represent?

options.A: Financial barrier
options.B: Language barrier
options.C: Transportation barrier
options.D: Side effect barrier

explanation: Adverse drug reactions such as nausea are common side effects that discourage patients from continuing their treatment unless managed properly. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h3)

question: What does 'trauma-informed care' mean when nursing a survivor of forced marriage?

options.A: Forcing the patient to recount every traumatic event immediately
options.B: Relying solely on medication to solve the patient's emotional pain
options.C: Allowing family members to make all medical decisions for the patient
options.D: Prioritizing the patient's safety, trust, and control in every interaction

explanation: Trauma-informed care centers on rebuilding the patient's sense of safety, empowerment, and trust in healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why is it dangerous to administer a medication prepared by another nurse?

options.A: It takes away valuable learning time from student nurses
options.B: The pharmacy software will crash when scanning the barcode
options.C: You cannot verify its true contents or preparation accuracy
options.D: It violates hospital laundry and uniform policies

explanation: The person who prepares the medication must be the one who administers it to maintain complete safety accountability. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h3)

question: What grooming tip should a nurse give to a patient on long-term blood thinners?

options.A: Use an electric razor instead of a blade
options.B: Stop all dental hygiene care to protect gums
options.C: Avoid brushing teeth to prevent minor bleeding
options.D: Shave with a traditional straight razor daily

explanation: Electric razors are much safer because they prevent accidental nicks and cuts that bleed easily on blood thinners. Smart advice! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h8)

question: Which sign strongly suggests a patient's sting site is developing a bacterial infection days later?

options.A: Spreading erythema, warmth, and purulent discharge at the site days later
options.B: Immediate localized pain and minor itching right after the sting
options.C: Clear fluid blisters that form and heal within twenty-four hours
options.D: A small drop in blood pressure within the first five minutes

explanation: Watch out for spreading redness (erythema), feeling hot to the touch, and pus (purulent discharge)—these are classic signs that bacteria have set in. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h7)

question: What is the main job of white blood cells when an infection enters the body?

options.A: To defend the body by neutralizing foreign invaders
options.B: To transport oxygen to body tissues
options.C: To digest food and absorb nutrients
options.D: To regulate blood pressure and fluid balance

explanation: Your white blood cells are your body's frontline military defenders, always on patrol to hunt down and destroy invading germs. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T2#GNS313_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why do hospitals carry out job performance evaluations for nurses?

options.A: To punish nurses who make minor documentation mistakes
options.B: To measure care quality and guide professional growth
options.C: To find reasons to reduce staff salaries each year
options.D: To replace daily supervision and peer feedback entirely

explanation: Evaluations aren't meant to witch-hunt! They help check how we are doing against professional standards so we can keep our patients safe and grow in our nursing careers. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h1)

question: Which factor most often decreases the effectiveness of short-acting hormonal methods like oral contraceptive pills?

options.A: Inconsistent daily use or missed doses by the client
options.B: The time of day the client eats her meals
options.C: The client's natural blood pressure levels
options.D: Using the pills during the winter months

explanation: Short-acting methods depend heavily on the user remembering to take or apply them on a strict schedule every day. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h5)

question: Why is deliberate silence often an effective nursing tool during end-of-life conversations?

options.A: It signals to the family that the conversation has ended
options.B: It gives the patient time to process heavy thoughts and emotions
options.C: It allows the nurse to document notes without interruption
options.D: It forces the patient to speak when they are feeling shy

explanation: End-of-life topics are emotionally heavy, and quiet moments allow patients the necessary time to gather their thoughts and speak when ready. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h1)

question: A patient is completely bedridden from a muscle disorder. Which bone problem are they most at risk for?

options.A: Sudden overproduction of red blood cells
options.B: Pathological bone fractures from decreased density
options.C: Involuntary muscle hypertrophy in the lower limbs
options.D: Drastic permanent height gain from spinal decompression

explanation: Bones need weight and pressure to stay strong. Staying in bed stops that pressure, making bones weak and fragile. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h3)

question: What term describes the natural slowing down of immune system function as a person grows older?

options.A: Immunodeficiency
options.B: Immunosenescence
options.C: Seroconversion
options.D: Hypersensitivity

explanation: Immunosenescence simply means 'immune aging.' Just like muscles get tired, our immune response naturally softens as we age. Great word to add to your nursing vocabulary! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T70#GNS214_U1_T70_h2)

question: An anterior gishiri cut most directly puts which structure at risk of injury?

options.A: The anal sphincter
options.B: The coccyx bone
options.C: The cervix
options.D: The urethra and bladder

explanation: Cutting the anterior vaginal wall risks damaging the urethra and bladder wall, leading to urinary fistula formation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h3)

question: What technology does an autoclave use to sterilize infectious medical waste?

options.A: Ultraviolet radiation
options.B: Pressurized steam
options.C: Open-air sun drying
options.D: Chemical bleach spray

explanation: Correct! Autoclaves use high heat and pressure to kill all germs on medical equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h7)

question: Which psychological condition is often seen in women and girls who have survived FGM?

options.A: Bipolar manic depression with hallucinations
options.B: Obsessive compulsive cleaning disorder
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder and anxiety
options.D: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder

explanation: Spot on! The painful and terrifying experience often leaves survivors with long-term emotional trauma, anxiety, and distress. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T1#GNS225_U6_T1_h5)

question: A patient with a fungal skin infection in the groin area asks how to prevent spreading it and getting it again. What should the nurse advise?

options.A: Apply thick occlusive petroleum jelly over the area all day
options.B: Wash the skin vigorously with harsh antiseptic soap every hour
options.C: Keep the skin folds clean and dry, and do not share towels
options.D: Wear heavy synthetic clothing to trap warm air near the skin

explanation: Fungi thrive in warm, moist places, so keeping the skin dry and avoiding shared personal items like towels stops transmission and growth. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why should a community health nurse look at clinic attendance data by gender?

options.A: To decide which patients get free medications
options.B: To fulfill paperwork requirements for the government
options.C: To determine which gender pays more in hospital taxes
options.D: To spot hidden barriers if one gender is missing from care

explanation: If sickness rates are equal but one gender never shows up at the clinic, it's a huge clue that a hidden barrier is stopping them. Excellent nursing logic! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h7)

question: A nurse is about to give a morning pill, but the patient's identification band is missing. What is the correct action?

options.A: Check the chart photo and give the medication to save time
options.B: Ask the patient to state their name and give the pill immediately
options.C: Ask another nurse to confirm the patient's face before giving the drug
options.D: Delay administration until a new identification band is placed on the patient

explanation: Two reliable identifiers like a properly fitted ID band are mandatory; guessing or relying solely on memory or roommates violates the right patient rule. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the main use of a partograph during childbirth?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of the hospital delivery
options.B: To document the complete family medical history of the father
options.C: To provide a visual record of the progress of labour and health status
options.D: To serve as a legal divorce document for the parents

explanation: You'll use the partograph daily in the maternity ward! It's simply a handy graph that helps you track how labour is flowing and keeps a close eye on both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h1)

question: Why is a non-judgmental approach so important when caring for a post-abortion client?

options.A: Clients often face stigma, fear, and guilt
options.B: It lowers the cost of medical supplies
options.C: It is required by the hospital billing department
options.D: It shortens the length of hospital stays

explanation: Many clients carry heavy emotional burdens like fear and societal stigma. A welcoming, open-hearted nurse helps build the trust they need to heal. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h1)

question: What is the best nursing action when caring for a pregnant woman with physiological anaemia?

options.A: Administer large doses of intravenous antibiotics immediately
options.B: Provide education on taking routine iron and folate supplements
options.C: Advise the patient to stop drinking water to thicken her blood
options.D: Prepare the patient for an emergency blood transfusion today

explanation: Routine antenatal iron and folate are key! As a nurse, teaching the mum how to take her supplements correctly makes all the difference. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h7)

question: How should you talk to a patient who has trouble hearing?

options.A: Shout loudly so the sound travels across the room
options.B: Whisper quietly directly into the patient's ear
options.C: Face the patient directly and speak in a normal tone
options.D: Use complex medical terms written on a notepad

explanation: Shouting actually distorts your words and makes lip-reading harder. Face them directly, speak clearly at a normal volume, and minimize background noise. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is a POSITIVE, 100% sure sign of pregnancy?

options.A: Missing your monthly period
options.B: A positive home pregnancy test
options.C: Morning sickness and vomiting
options.D: Hearing the baby's heartbeat on an ultrasound

explanation: When you actually hear or see that little heartbeat on an ultrasound, there's no guessing anymore—that's a confirmed pregnancy! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T001#GNS226_U2_T001_h6)

question: Why do nursing schools regularly ask students for feedback about their learning conditions?

options.A: To swap all hospital postings for online multiple-choice tests
options.B: To look for reasons to chase struggling students away
options.C: To find ways to improve the school and fix problems
options.D: To check which textbooks cost the most money

explanation: Your voice matters! Student feedback lets administrators know what is going well and what needs fixing in classrooms and wards. [learn more](GST321_U8_T3#GST321_U8_T3_h8)

question: What is the main job of the circulating nurse during an operation?

options.A: Closing the surgical wound layers with sutures and staples
options.B: Managing the unsterile environment and monitoring patient safety
options.C: Performing the surgical incisions alongside the primary surgeon
options.D: Administering the general anesthetic gases to the patient

explanation: While the scrub nurse is sterile at the table, the circulating nurse moves freely around the room to coordinate supplies, record notes, and watch out for the patient's safety. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h3)

question: A patient's heart rate is 42 beats per minute, and they feel dizzy with low blood pressure. Which emergency drug should the nurse expect to give?

options.A: Atropine
options.B: Metoprolol
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Digoxin

explanation: Atropine is the go-to emergency medication used to block vagal slowing and quickly bring up a dangerously low, symptomatic heart rate. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h6)

question: Why is drug-resistant TB so much harder to treat than regular TB?

options.A: Second-line drugs are more toxic, expensive, and require longer treatment courses
options.B: Patients with resistant TB no longer need to take medications every day
options.C: Resistant bacteria do not cause any symptoms, making patients ignore treatment
options.D: Second-line drugs only work when injected directly into the lung tissue

explanation: Backup drugs come with heavier side effects, cost more, and take much longer to work, making patient support super important. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why do we call Ebola a zoonotic disease?

options.A: It spreads exclusively among wild animals in the forest
options.B: It can only be transmitted through contaminated water
options.C: It mutates rapidly inside human respiratory tracts
options.D: It originates in animals and spreads to humans

explanation: You got it! 'Zoonotic' simply means an infection that jumps from animals to humans. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h1)

question: A patient refuses a bath because the bathroom feels cold and confusing. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Scold the patient for being uncooperative with personal hygiene
options.B: Cancel all future baths indefinitely to avoid upsetting the patient
options.C: Warm the room, simplify the process, and break it down into gentle steps
options.D: Force the patient into the tub immediately to maintain hygiene standards

explanation: Making the environment cozy and taking things slow helps ease fear and resistance during personal care. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h6)

question: Which lab test is usually ordered to check if hormones are causing a patient's sexual difficulties?

options.A: Serum calcium
options.B: Serum testosterone
options.C: Urinalysis culture
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: You got it! Checking serum testosterone levels lets us see if low hormone production is the culprit behind the struggle. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T24#GNS312_U1_T24_h5)

question: A nurse studies post-operative pain and uses a numeric pain rating scale to collect data. What is that pain scale?

options.A: The overarching strategy
options.B: The conceptual framework
options.C: A research method
options.D: The research design

explanation: You're getting it! The pain scale is a specific tool used to gather information, making it a research method. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T2#GNS224_U1_T2_h3)

question: A nurse is teaching breathing techniques to a patient with severe lung fibrosis. Which method should the nurse demonstrate to help ease shortness of breath?

options.A: Holding the breath for two minutes after each deep sigh
options.B: Breathing exclusively through the mouth while running fast
options.C: Rapid shallow panting to increase carbon dioxide retention
options.D: Pursed-lip breathing to help keep airways open longer

explanation: Pursed-lip breathing creates gentle backpressure in the airways, preventing them from collapsing prematurely and easing shortness of breath. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h6)

question: What should you do if your sterile collection swab accidentally touches the patient's bed sheet?

options.A: Wipe it clean with an alcohol swab and use it
options.B: Proceed with the test because sheets are clean
options.C: Discard the contaminated swab and get a new one
options.D: Blow on the tip to remove any invisible dust

explanation: Once a sterile item touches a non-sterile surface like a bed sheet, it's no longer sterile. Toss it and grab a fresh one—patient safety first! [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h8)

question: What does the letter 'A' stand for in the emergency assessment framework ABCDE?

options.A: Activity
options.B: Airway
options.C: Anxiety
options.D: Antibiotic

explanation: Checking the airway is always the first step in any emergency to make sure air can flow freely into the lungs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h6)

question: What type of food should make up the biggest part of an adolescent girl's daily energy intake?

options.A: Refined table sugars
options.B: Pure protein powders
options.C: Saturated animal fats
options.D: Complex carbohydrates

explanation: Wonderful! Complex carbs (like yam, brown rice, and beans) give growing teens steady, lasting energy and healthy fiber. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T010#GNS227_U2_T010_h4)

question: How would you best describe depression in a clinical setting?

options.A: A temporary lack of vitamins causing physical weakness
options.B: A minor behavioral adjustment issue in older adults
options.C: A serious mood disorder affecting thoughts and daily activities
options.D: A temporary emotional reaction to physical fatigue

explanation: Spot on! Depression isn't just a brief bad mood or fatigue; it's a true mood disorder that impacts a person's entire daily life and well-being. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why might a quiet, withdrawn patient still be dealing with serious fear?

options.A: Fear can cause behavioral withdrawal and freezing instead of crying out.
options.B: Withdrawn patients have completely empty minds.
options.C: Silence always proves that a patient is fully relaxed.
options.D: Quiet patients never experience the fight-or-flight response.

explanation: Well done! Not everyone screams or cries when scared. Some patients freeze, shut down, or go completely quiet when they are overwhelmed. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T11#GNS123_U3_T11_h4)

question: What do biological theories of aging primarily focus on?

options.A: Social interaction and community roles
options.B: Cellular damage and physical wear-and-tear
options.C: Retirement patterns and financial security
options.D: Emotional adjustment to loss

explanation: Biological theories look at physical changes, genetics, and cellular breakdown as the drivers of aging. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the very first step of urine formation in the kidney?

options.A: Tubular secretion
options.B: Glomerular filtration
options.C: Peristaltic propulsion
options.D: Tubular reabsorption

explanation: Everything starts at the glomerulus! Blood pressure forces water and small particles out of the blood and into Bowman's capsule to kick off urine making. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T1#GNS213_U4_T1_h4)

question: In which patient situation is an expectorant the absolute best choice?

options.A: Bacterial pneumonia requiring broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics
options.B: A dry, irritating nighttime cough that keeps the patient awake
options.C: Acute bronchitis with thick, difficult-to-cough-up phlegm
options.D: Severe bronchospasm during an acute asthma attack

explanation: Correct! When a patient has heavy bronchitis with stubborn, thick phlegm stuck in their chest, an expectorant is just what they need. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T3#GNS223_U2_T3_h4)

question: A relative has spent three days straight at the bedside without sleeping or eating well. What should you do?

options.A: Scold the relative for neglecting their own physical health
options.B: Tell security to remove the relative from the facility
options.C: Ignore the behavior since staying vigilant is completely normal
options.D: Gently encourage periods of rest and offer assistance from support services

explanation: Caregiver exhaustion is very real. Gently remind them to step away for a meal or a nap so they don't break down too. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T8#GNS221_U4_T8_h4)

question: Why do we teach pursed-lip breathing to patients with chronic lung issues?

options.A: It lowers the patient's blood pressure immediately
options.B: It stops all coughing episodes within a few minutes
options.C: It replaces the need for using oxygen therapy
options.D: It keeps airways open longer and helps expel trapped air

explanation: Well done! Breathing out through pursed lips creates a gentle back-pressure, stopping tiny airways from collapsing too soon. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h8)

question: Which management theory focuses the most on efficiency, timing tasks, and standard work routines?

options.A: Human Relations Theory
options.B: Democratic Leadership Theory
options.C: Chaos Management Theory
options.D: Scientific Management

explanation: Scientific management looks closely at how tasks are done to cut out wasted time and make every action as efficient as possible. [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the main reason nurses ask patients to take off all jewelry and hairpins before an MRI?

options.A: To keep the changing rooms clean and organized
options.B: To prevent static electricity from building up on clothing
options.C: To stop the patient from losing valuables during the test
options.D: To prevent metal objects from turning into dangerous projectiles

explanation: Spot on! That giant magnet can pull loose metal items like a flying bullet, which could hurt someone or break the machine. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h4)

question: A patient with low iron levels eats plenty of beans and spinach. What advice should the nurse give to improve iron absorption?

options.A: Cook the vegetables in a microwave without water
options.B: Drink fresh orange juice or eat tomatoes with the meal
options.C: Drink a cup of strong black tea right after eating
options.D: Take the iron food with a glass of whole milk

explanation: Orange juice and tomatoes are rich in vitamin C, which enhances the absorption of non-heme iron found in plants. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which of these is an example of an environmental reservoir of infection?

options.A: A healthcare worker with a mild cold
options.B: An asymptomatic human carrier
options.C: A stray dog carrying the rabies virus
options.D: Contaminated soil and water supplies

explanation: Things around us like soil, water, and food are non-living environmental sources where certain germs love to hide and grow. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h2)

question: A nurse organizes a community screening program to check blood sugar levels in adults over forty. Which level of prevention does this represent?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Screenings are designed to find hidden health problems early so treatment can start right away, which is secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which skin antiseptic keeps working for hours after you apply it?

options.A: Glutaraldehyde
options.B: Sodium hypochlorite
options.C: Chlorhexidine gluconate
options.D: Isopropyl alcohol

explanation: Spot on! Chlorhexidine sticks to the skin and keeps killing bacteria long after you put it on, which is why we love it for surgical scrubs. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h3)

question: You just received a delivery of delicate protein medications for your ward. What is your very first priority?

options.A: Place the vials in a warm blanket warmer to activate them
options.B: Store them openly on the nurse's station desk for easy access
options.C: Crush the vials to prepare liquid doses for oral feeding tubes
options.D: Check and follow the required cold-chain refrigeration rules

explanation: Biotech protein drugs are super fragile! They'll lose their potency quickly if they aren't kept at the right cold temperature right away. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h8)

question: What is the main focus of epidemiology in healthcare?

options.A: Treating rare surgical conditions in tertiary hospitals
options.B: Managing hospital finances and staff rosters
options.C: Performing laboratory tests on individual blood samples
options.D: Studying how and why diseases occur in populations

explanation: Spot on! While bedside nursing looks at one patient at a time, epidemiology zooms out to look at health patterns across entire communities. You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h1)

question: A community nurse visits a stroke survivor weekly to check skin integrity and assist with arm exercises. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primordial prevention
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: Helping an existing stroke patient recover movement and prevent complications like bedsores is tertiary care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h4)

question: What do we call the normal vaginal discharge that a mother passes as her uterus heals after birth?

options.A: Lochia
options.B: Colostrum
options.C: Leukorrhea
options.D: Smegma

explanation: Lochia is just the body's natural way of cleaning out the uterus after delivery—shedding old tissue and blood as healing takes place. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h3)

question: You ask a patient to touch their own nose and then touch your finger over and over. What are you testing?

options.A: Superficial pain perception
options.B: Cerebellar coordination
options.C: Cranial nerve vision
options.D: Deep tendon reflexes

explanation: The finger-to-nose test checks the cerebellum, which is the part of the brain that keeps your body movements smooth and coordinated. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why are fallopian tubes easily reached by infections starting in the lower vagina or cervix?

options.A: They lack any blood supply to fight off invading microorganisms
options.B: They produce constant secretions that feed bacterial pathogens
options.C: They share a continuous open mucosal pathway with the uterus and cervix
options.D: They are located outside the main pelvic cavity entirely

explanation: Because the female reproductive tract is an open road from the vagina up through the uterus and tubes, bacteria can easily travel upward. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h1)

question: Which injection is routinely given during antenatal care to protect the newborn from tetanus?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Tetanus toxoid vaccine
options.C: Iron and folic acid tablets
options.D: Antimalarial drugs

explanation: Wonderful! Giving the tetanus toxoid vaccine to pregnant women helps build immunity that passes straight to the baby, keeping neonatal tetanus away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h2)

question: What is a major challenge in providing adolescent reproductive care in many communities?

options.A: The requirement that all nurses undergo legal training before practice
options.B: A complete lack of teenage patients visiting urban health facilities
options.C: Conflict between traditional moral disapproval and young people's health needs
options.D: An absolute nationwide ban on importing any modern contraceptive items

explanation: Cultural and religious beliefs often clash with the clinical reality that teens need reproductive health support. Navigating this is part of nursing! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T10#GNS312_U3_T10_h8)

question: In pharmacokinetics, what does the letter 'A' stand for in the famous ADME acronym?

options.A: Acidification
options.B: Absorption
options.C: Anabolism
options.D: Agglutination

explanation: Think of ADME as the journey of a drug in the body: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion. You've got this! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T1#GNS125_U5_T1_h1)

question: How can health facilities best fix the problem of staff underreporting due to a fear of blame?

options.A: By firing every nurse who makes a minor documentation error
options.B: By hiding all disease statistics from the government ministry
options.C: By stopping all surveillance activities during busy seasons
options.D: By fostering a supportive, blame-free work culture that values data

explanation: When staff know they won't be unfairly punished for honest mistakes, they are much more open and accurate with their reporting. Spot on! [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h8)

question: In midwifery, what does the term 'gravidity' mean?

options.A: The number of surgical deliveries performed
options.B: The total number of times a woman has been pregnant
options.C: The number of children currently living at home
options.D: The total weight of all babies delivered

explanation: Think of gravidity as the pregnancy counter! It counts every single time a woman has been pregnant, no matter how the pregnancy ended. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T3#GNS311_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why can't steroid hormones be stored inside small cellular sacs (vesicles) before use?

options.A: They must be manufactured immediately by red blood cells
options.B: They are fat-soluble and easily diffuse right through cell membranes
options.C: They are too large to fit inside standard intracellular vesicles
options.D: They react violently with water stored inside cellular compartments

explanation: Because steroid hormones love fats, they slip right through cell walls like ghosts! That means cells can't trap them in little sacs—they just make them fresh whenever the body needs them. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T1#GNS222_U2_T1_h3)

question: A client with diabetes calls the clinic feeling nauseous and vomiting with a mild fever. What is the best advice to give them?

options.A: Stop taking all diabetes medications immediately until your stomach settles down
options.B: Continue taking your insulin, drink plenty of fluids, and check your blood sugar often
options.C: Restrict all fluid intake for the next twelve hours to prevent vomiting episodes
options.D: Double your oral diabetes pills to clear out the excess toxins causing the fever

explanation: When patients are sick, stress hormones naturally push blood sugar up. Remind them: never stop insulin during illness, and keep pushing those fluids! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h8)

question: Which of these is a key nursing check during routine postnatal care?

options.A: Surgically repairing minor perineal tears after 6 weeks
options.B: Administering the BCG vaccine to the mother
options.C: Measuring the child's head circumference daily
options.D: Checking uterine involution and lochia flow

explanation: Well done! Monitoring how the uterus shrinks (involution) and the type of lochia helps you catch postpartum bleeding or infection early. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h5)
